th 06/Dated: 30 January, 2026 I.A. No.14515 of 2025
1. Heard Mr. Jagdeesh, learned counsel for the appellant and learned P.P. for the State.
2.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail to him during pendency of this appeal.

3. The appellant has been convicted for the offences under Sections 363, 376(3) and 376(DA) of Indian Penal Code and Section 6 of POCSO Act and has been sentenced to imprisonment for life,
which shall mean imprisonment for remainder of natural life along with a fine of Rs.25,000/- for the offence under section 6 of POCSO Act.
4. It has been alleged that the appellant and another convict had committed rape upon the victim.
5. Submission has been advanced by learned counsel for the appellant that the evidence of the victim (P.W.1) suffers from serious contradictions and infirmities.
It has further been submitted that the appellant is in custody since 18.04.2023.

sentences.text:
6. Learned P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant and has submitted that the prayer for bail of one of the co-convicts, Kandey Birua has already been rejected by this Court in Cr. Appeal (D.B.) No.666 of 2025.
7.
It appears that the victim has been examined as P.W.1 in which she has categorically stated about the involvement of the appellant in committing rape upon her along with co-convict, Kandey Birua.
The medical report is also supportive of the factum of the rape committed upon the victim.
8. Regarding being had to the aforesaid facts, we are not inclined to admit the appellant on bail.
The prayer for bail of the appellant is, hereby, rejected.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) 30/01/2026 Pappu/-
